timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Thank you. Hello, everyone. I'm Maris. I'm a Latvian diplomat here in New York, and I am working here on gender issues and
I am a vice chair of the CSW Bureau, which is the Commission on Status of Women. And indeed this year we had to also renew or methods of work. The methods of work is a resolution that establishes the
basic rules of how the Commission functions. And indeed this year we managed to had an addition in the methods of work.
And this addition is that now there will be an interactive dialogue with the youth as an official part of the program. So every spring the Commission meets and
hold its session and there are different dialogues and events in the official program. There are dialogues with experts.
There are ministers coming to New York giving speeches. And now there will be also the interactive dialogue with youth about the process how we how we got it in the methods of work.
So 193 countries have to negotiate the methods of work. And states have different relationships with civil society, not all states like to hear what civil society and youth has to say.

But there are also countries that set your voice as a priority. So in the room when we negotiate the methods of work all these countries came together. And I had the difficult task of facilitating the negotiations, which meant that we meet in the room for many years.

And so many many hours and all these countries with their different interests try to find the common ground that they could agree on. So there were very supportive countries of including the youth dialogue who have clearly set it in their negotiation strategies to to have the interactive dialogue in the end.
So there are a lot of countries of course that strongly opposed it. So what do we have in the end. So we have the interactive dialogue included in the methods of work.
And the middle ground that the countries were able to find is that the youth that will be speaking in the interactive dialogue dialogue will be from the delegations of the member states.
And the compromise because that way we have the interactive dialogue, but countries have some control over who will exactly speak on it.

So during the interactive dialogue, meaning that those countries who are afraid of what the youth might say at such an event, if they are invited, they have a control because they can send, I know, no, a youth representative that will not say anything controversial or something that the country will not like.
And so the nature of the nature of you and we have to find compromises.
UN is a platform well all countries, no matter how different they look at the world, no matter how different their cultures and national policies are.

This is the platform where everyone comes together and try to find a common ground, something that everyone can agree upon. And it is inevitably something that is not necessarily the most progressive of ideas.
About more concrete modalities, I will be happy to come back to you in a few months because in, in autumn is when the UN women.
And the CSW bureau come together and and and start to very specifically organize the session.
The next session, the 67 session, and then we will see.

The methods of work say that this interactive dialogue will fall off the modalities for interactive dialogues and meaning that we already have interactive dialogues with scientists and others. So it will fall off the same rules and arrangements, which means that it will be like an hour and a half event.

It also looks like that it will fall off the same kind of invitation process, meaning that you and women will probably taking into account geographical distribution and other considerations, propose to the commission.

Which countries could speak, which you like youth from which countries could speak at the interactive dialogue because we cannot in hour and a half how 193 representatives giving speech so it will be very difficult decisions to make.
So it is transparent as much as possible and and fair to the to the global community of youth who will be represented at this event.
But let's meet in autumn again and and I will have more to to say about that.
